title: Why I Redesigned My Portfolio – From Inspiration to Identity
excerpt: That old portfolio? Definitely not me. This one lives in Night Owl, like the rest of my brain.
author: Yassine Bouali
content:
The old portfolio wasn't really mine.
It was someone else's layout I liked enough to borrow.
Nothing wrong with that — but it never felt personal.

So I started over.
I wanted something that actually feels like me.
Something built from scratch, with my own flow and my own voice.
No borrowed pieces this time.

Just clean, honest lines that tell my story.

### The Night Owl Shift

I spend 90% of my time inside an IDE (specifically, with the Night Owl theme). It's calm, it's focused, and the syntax highlighting makes sense.
I realized my portfolio shouldn't just be a corporate landing page; it should reflect the environment where I do my best work.

So I brought the editor to the web.

```typescript
const me = {
  role: "Software Engineer",
  focus: ["Backend", "AI/RAG", "Industrial IT"],
  status: "Building",
};
```

This is me now.
Welcome inside.

title: I Built and Published My Own Python Library
excerpt: I kept repeating the same configuration and logging setup across projects, so I decided to turn it into a reusable Python package.
author: Yassine Bouali
content:
I kept writing the same configuration and logging setup across different Python projects.

At some point, I thought: why am I rebuilding this every time?

So I decided to extract it into a proper Python library: **yb-observability**.

### From project code to a package

The goal was simple: have reusable infrastructure that I could install in different Python applications instead of maintaining another copy of the same code.

The library currently focuses on two things:

- Configuration loading and environment variable handling
- Consistent application logging with Loguru

`python
from yb_observability.config import ConfigLoader

config = ConfigLoader("config/config.yml").load()
`

Nothing revolutionary. Just infrastructure that should be boring, predictable, and reusable.

### Making it real

I didn't want it to stay as another internal utility sitting inside one of my projects.

So I packaged it properly, added tests and quality checks, set up CI, and published it to **PyPI**.

Now it can actually be installed and used by other Python projects.

`bash
pip install yb-observability
`

That part was probably more satisfying than writing the library itself.

### Why I built it

This project is also a small step toward treating my own tooling more seriously.

Instead of keeping useful pieces hidden inside application repositories, I want to extract the parts that are genuinely reusable, document them, test them, and make them available as independent packages.

**yb-observability** is the first step in that direction.

It is small, but it is real: an open-source Python project, published on PyPI, that I can now use across my own applications and continue improving over time.
